timing.description: Decision = submission of a pre-signed ladder order ~150 ms before its match, on the Binance spot book read ~80-110 ms after the stamp (knee at 230-260 ms before the match on exchange time). At that clock the take is largely decoded: a 50-ms hazard reaches AUC 0.8885 vs 0.7591 for Polymarket activity (per wallet DS 0.8812, GF 0.9028, XM 0.9191); top inputs the 100 / 250-ms spot microprice return toward o and |p - 0.5|. Only ~8% of decisions follow a price-level tick (placebo 1.2%); the rest follow sub-tick queue-imbalance moves. Follower legs 180-220 ms later are re-decisions on fresher spot (86% at their own anchor vs 79%). An operator-level 30-60-s activity state remains (iteration 12). Block-second presence 0.870 vs a capture-aware market baseline 0.846 (+0.024): at the block clock the crowd's co-arrivals reveal most of the operator's takes. The fast crowd's co-takes in the same 50-ms knee band are explained 53% by the knee-clock design (iteration 12: 14-21%). Own-state kernels of past decisions add only +0.01 AUC at the knee clock (iteration 12: +0.037). Iteration 15: the Polymarket book carries the same timing information: a market-only baseline with the capture's book depth and its 100-ms changes at the bot's view reaches 0.8730 against the decoded hazard's 0.8808 (book only 0.8706; on own-print-clean bins 0.910 vs 0.912); the makers cancel o's asks on the same Binance move ~before the operator's order arrives, and the operator takes what is left. Take rate by top deciles: both channels 6.2%, book only 1.9%, spot only 1.5%, neither 0.2%. Book cut scan: the makers' matching cancels arrive within ~50 ms of the bot's own view; with the book cut at e (PIT for every label) the hazard's gain over the book-aware baseline is +0.058 [0.050, 0.065], at e + 50 +0.008. Iteration 17: the knee transfers out of time (live, 11-01): first legs' spot tick lock peaks 255 ms before the match (DS 255, GF 285; capture 265 / 285).

Pre-registered (pre-registration 5), fitted on 10-17..19 and scored once on 10-20..22: 0.8369 per taker order (DS 0.8306, GF 0.8547, XM 0.8132), 0.8236 per decision, 88 / 87 / 84 / 78 / 69% by window minute; market-only 0.568, own-inventory 0.539, placebo 0.50, old anchor 0.742; the information arrives in a 60-ms band and nothing is added after it; no knee for the non-co-arriving crowd. Exam route dc_exam14 (capture day files). Late decisions (after 180 s) mix weaker tick-following and own-state pairing. Iteration 15: the Polymarket book of both outcomes at m0 - 210 gives the side at 0.712 alone and is right on 62% of the orders dc14 gets wrong; dc14 + book 0.838 vs dc14 0.8135 per order on 10-21..22 (designed and scored once, not pre-registered). price.description: Limit = o's ask the bot saw (DS's view in (m - 250, m - 180] on the book clock, complete 10-20 calldata) plus 0 c for a small order and +1 c (or more) for a large one: DS small 0 c 94%, DS large +1 c 60% / +2..3 c 21%; GF small 0 c 66%, GF large +1 c 84%; XM spreads +0 / +1 / +2..3 (iteration 16). The per-wallet anchor of iteration 13 (DS 0, GF 1, XM 1 c; out of sample 0.937 pooled) is mostly the per-wallet large share. o's ask at m - 180 within a tick 90.7% live, 95.1% on VALIDATE calldata (trivial touch anchor, stated as such); lost races are the decisions priced on an ask that moved during the hold. Iteration 17 new regime: XM sends 60-share BUY orders from the same pre-signed ladder (3-18 per window, both outcomes) that never take: they are priced at the ask of the bot's view (ask == L 100 ms before they appear in the book in 63%) and rest as the new best bid one tick below the moved ask (lost races of the late slot, or post-only orders at the ask), filled a median 9 s later; their side follows the frozen dc14 rule at 0.80 [VALIDATE-only, development block 11-01].

size.description: Iteration 16, on the COMPLETE calldata record of 10-20..22 (every operator taker order's original size): the ORIGINAL size is a large (100) / small (30) class with per-wallet base rates outside size phases (DS 3.8%, GF 32%, XM 34% on 10-20; size phases of hours raise every wallet, e.g. 10-19 01-13 h, 10-20 19 h), repeated on the side of the operator's realized large lean (GF / XM: P(large) ~0.5 with no lean, 0.51-0.59 with it, 0.13-0.15 against it = the small pairing stream), and coupled with the price (large orders priced ask + 1 c or more, small at the ask). DS's large class is public at AUC 0.77-0.84 (the 250-ms spot move at its own anchor, the book at its own view, an ask already moving toward o); GF / XM's is public at only 0.62-0.70 and own-lean driven (0.71-0.78 from the lean alone). The REALIZED taker fill is execution on the post-hold book: min(original, o's ask depth <= L ~35 ms before the match) at r 0.895 on all 27,008 orders of 10-20 (0.50 at the bot's view). A replica's own simulated lean carries no information on the size realizations (pre-registration 10 (b) failed). Carrier allocation: a fixed priority list over in-flight orders with a ~300-ms slot, DS > GF > (W4) > XM (0.778 of the three wallets' carriers on visible occupancy; with W4 / W5 as slots DS > GF > W4 > XM > W5 is best and 36.6% of XM-led first legs follow a W4 / W5 leg within 300 ms), with unseen lost legs ahead of GF / XM-led legs. The public book's cancel wave before a decision names XM's overflow legs at AUC 0.83 (true decision density 0.84), lifting XM's PnL ceiling to ~0.49-0.50 (iteration 16, not pre-registered). Iteration 17: the class is a decision-level variable whose RATE and carrier LIST are configuration (11-01: GF 0.08 vs 0.27, pooled first-leg large share 0.053 vs 0.083, large first legs GF 0.24 vs 0.53); within a regime it follows the operator's decision memory (S = side of its last large order, E = commitment; S-relation AUC 0.84-0.88 for fast followers), and the side of every large order is public (dc14 0.878, seeds 0.918), but WHICH decisions are large is a coin a replica cannot synchronize (own-memory agreement 0.55, window-net r +0.015 / +0.043 over the menu; pre-registration 12 failed). Class-keyed lists (small DS > GF > XM, large GF > DS > XM) name 0.656 of large carriers (size-blind 0.540).

exit.description: Remainders and lost races rest as GTC bids at the old ask (cancelled never-filled remainders live DS median 328 ms, GF 240, XM 124); every position is held to resolution; 87% of shares end paired at 0.979; TAKER_REBATE = 0.5 x the previous day's taker fees. Iteration 12, the INVENTORY PATH: per window PnL = net x outcome (r 0.884); the net follows the current minute's BTC move (+), is bought back against the earlier minutes' moves (-) and leans with the previous window's outcome (+); public models predict the window net at r 0.46-0.48 (market activity alone 0.34), and an executable exposure tracker that buys the predicted net deficit with strict fills (latency >= 2 s) reproduces the per-window PnL at Pearson 0.476 / Spearman 0.440 (GF 0.34, DS 0.43, XM 0.06; market-only tracker 0.36 / 0.32); the wallets' per-window PnLs are nearly independent of each other (0.00-0.20). Iteration 13: the inventory path is two operator-level streams, a large-size lean (cross-wallet r 0.35-0.47) and a small-size taker counter-flow that buys back the REALIZED large inventory (within-wallet corr(L, S) -0.26..-0.60; dose-dependent pairing, t -26.5); public data predicts L at r 0.32 and the counter-flow residual at ~0.3, and a two-stream target adds nothing to the window-net prediction (0.4195 vs 0.4237). Per-wallet PnL is bounded by dispatch: XM <= 0.30-0.41 under every pooled-stream oracle. Iteration 14: a millisecond nowcast (nfms14) and a decision-hazard nowcast do not lift the tracker (pre-registrations 6 / 7); XM's PnL is a random thinning of the operator's decisions (oracle 0.3925, redraw ceiling 0.4304 < 0.47). Iteration 15: the depth-weighted hazard nowcast (pre-registration 8) does not lift the tracker (mix15 0.4772 / 0.4556 vs mix14 0.4792 / 0.4594 on 576 windows of 10-21..22). Iteration 17: a two-phase target does not lift the tracker (pre-registration 13: 0.5064 / 0.4675 vs 0.5065 / 0.4674). In the new regime XM's PnL is its maker stream (86% of its shares are maker fills), which the taker-only tracker does not trade.

strategy_statement: One operator runs a TypeScript clob-client bot on three (plus a fourth and a fifth) wallets in every BTC 5-minute Up/Down window, and only there [VALIDATE-only]. It pre-signs BUY orders on both outcomes at every cent in bursts 13-120 s ahead (1.66 ms per cent whatever the number of sizes per cent, so the signing is parallel or the timestamps are scheduled; the salts are not V8 Math.random output of nearby calls) [VALIDATE-only]. It sits next to Polymarket's engine and reads the Binance SPOT book ~80-110 ms after Binance stamps it; when the spot microprice shifts toward an outcome over the last ~100-250 ms it submits a pre-signed order at the ask it saw ~30-70 ms before arriving [VALIDATE-only]; the side is 0.8369 per taker order on the pre-registered split [VALIDATE-only]. Each decision goes to the first free wallet in a fixed priority list DS > GF > W4 > XM (> W5; W4 / W5 are the operator's other wallets), a wallet staying busy ~300 ms after its submission whether its order fills or not; GF- and XM-led legs are often a later slot behind lost legs nobody sees (tick lock shifted by the slot gaps; DS remainders exactly one cent below GF's limit; 37% of XM-led first legs follow a W4 / W5 leg within 300 ms) [VALIDATE-only]. The size is a large / small class with per-wallet base rates (DS ~4%, GF / XM ~32-34%), repeated on the side of the operator's realized large lean and priced one cent above the ask when large; DS's large class is predictable from public data (AUC ~0.8), GF's and XM's mostly from the operator's own realized lean [VALIDATE-only]. Polymarket holds every marketable order 150 ms; the makers cancel most of the depth the bot saw, and the order fills min(size, depth left ~35 ms before the match) (r 0.895) [VALIDATE-only]. Lost races rest at the old ask and sometimes fill as maker [VALIDATE-only]. Positions are held to resolution; most shares end paired; about half the profit is the taker-fee rebate [VALIDATE-only]. The window PnL is the size of the large lean: public data predicts it at r ~0.5 (exposure tracker 0.5065 / 0.4674 on 10-20..22), because the size realizations are coins conditioned on the operator's own realized lean, which a replica's own state cannot reproduce; which wallet carries a decision follows the dispatcher, and with the operator's occupancy or its local decision density known XM's PnL ceiling is 0.51-0.62 (0.43-0.46 under a lottery), but the public hazard does not reproduce that density (0.48) [VALIDATE-only]. Nothing is exam-verified yet. ITERATION 17 [VALIDATE-only unless noted]: out of time, in the 11-01 regime, the knee (255 ms) and the taker routing transfer, the frozen side route scores 0.72-0.75 on a live laptop feed whose clock drifts (not 0.80; the score moves ~5 points per 25 ms of clock mapping) [out-of-time development check], the large-class rate and list are configuration (GF 0.08 vs 0.27), and XM's fills became 92% maker fills from 60-share orders (a component last seen on 10-09..13 and absent from the whole VALIDATE week) that are the same decisions (dc14 side 0.80) priced at the ask of the bot's view and resting after the ask moved (lost races of the late slot, or post-only orders) [development block 11-01]. The size class is drawn per decision on the side the dc14 rule predicts (0.88) and kept by the operator's decision memory (side of its last large order); which decisions are large is a coin that a replica's own memory does not reproduce (pre-registration 12 failed).
